headline: Town Council resolution urges restoring 17 classrooms in high school consolidation project
summary: The resolution says teachers and school staff strongly advocated for the 17 additional classrooms and asks the board to reverse its decision and restore them. A motion to add the resolution to the Operations agenda failed, 4-5. Public speakers asked the board to review a proposal on how the Lyman Hall homecoming dance was handled. Members also approved a $45,000 transfer from contingency to the professional and legal fees account for an FOI complaint.
decisions: Approved consent agenda items 7.1 to 7.13, except 7.3.3 and 7.3.5.
Approved transfer of $45,000 from contingency to professional and legal fees, with one vote against and one recusal.
Approved consent item 7.3.3, Colliers Addendum and Geotech study, with one vote opposed.
Denied adding the Town Council resolution on high school classrooms to the Operations agenda, 4-5.
Accepted the retirement of Ralph Eric Stratman, effective December 5th, 2026.
Approved unpaid leave of absence for Brian Farrell from December 8th, 2026 through February 12th, 2027.
discussion: High school project resolution: Members debated whether the Town Council resolution should be added to the agenda, and some said its views should be acknowledged. The motion failed 4-5.
High school project comments: A speaker agreed with the resolution and said the back-and-forth over the project had begun to tear the town apart.

Homecoming dance policy: Public speakers asked the board to review a proposal on the Lyman Hall homecoming dance, saying some students were turned away while later arrivals got in. Administration said an investigation had started and the recommendations would be reviewed.

FOI complaint legal fees: Members questioned why costs passed the earlier $20,000 estimate and whether $45,000 would be enough. Bills through the end of October totaled $32,938.90, and any money not spent can go back to contingency.
